title: May Restock Priorities
summary: Identify the top 5 products that should be restocked in May to support sales in June and July, based on sales trends across all stores. Focus on products with strong seasonal demand, rising trends, or recurring stock pressure.
executed_sql_queries:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_date)::int AS sales_year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date)::int AS sales_month,
  COUNT(*) AS order_item_rows,
  SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold,
  SUM(oi.total_amount) AS revenue
FROM retail.orders o
JOIN retail.order_items oi
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (2, 3, 4, 5)
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

WITH monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    oi.product_id,
    p.product_name,
    p.sku,
    p.category_id,
    p.type_id,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS month,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS monthly_units_sold,
    SUM(oi.total_amount) AS monthly_revenue
  FROM retail.order_items oi
  JOIN retail.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN retail.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
  WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2025-02-01'
    AND o.order_date < DATE '2025-08-01'
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6
)
SELECT *
FROM monthly_sales
ORDER BY monthly_units_sold DESC, monthly_revenue DESC
LIMIT 50;

WITH monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    oi.product_id,
    p.product_name,
    p.sku,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS month,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS monthly_units_sold,
    SUM(oi.total_amount) AS monthly_revenue
  FROM retail.order_items oi
  JOIN retail.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN retail.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
  WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2025-02-01'
    AND o.order_date < DATE '2025-08-01'
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
), product_totals AS (
  SELECT product_id, product_name, sku, SUM(monthly_units_sold) AS total_units_sold
  FROM monthly_sales
  GROUP BY 1,2,3
), ranked AS (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC, product_id) AS rn
  FROM product_totals
)
SELECT *
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 5
ORDER BY rn;

WITH top_products AS (
  SELECT 24 AS product_id UNION ALL
  SELECT 17 UNION ALL
  SELECT 9 UNION ALL
  SELECT 3 UNION ALL
  SELECT 27
), monthly_sales AS (
  SELECT
    oi.product_id,
    p.product_name,
    p.sku,
    DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)::date AS month,
    SUM(oi.quantity) AS monthly_units_sold,
    SUM(oi.total_amount) AS monthly_revenue
  FROM retail.order_items oi
  JOIN retail.orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
  JOIN retail.products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
  WHERE o.order_date >= DATE '2025-02-01'
    AND o.order_date < DATE '2025-08-01'
    AND oi.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM top_products)
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
SELECT *
FROM monthly_sales
ORDER BY product_id, month;

WITH top_products AS (
  SELECT 24 AS product_id UNION ALL
  SELECT 17 UNION ALL
  SELECT 9 UNION ALL
  SELECT 3 UNION ALL
  SELECT 27
)
SELECT
  i.store_id,
  s.store_name,
  s.is_online,
  i.product_id,
  p.product_name,
  p.sku,
  i.stock_level
FROM retail.inventory i
JOIN retail.stores s ON s.store_id = i.store_id
JOIN retail.products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id
WHERE i.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM top_products)
ORDER BY i.product_id, i.stock_level ASC, i.store_id;

components.content:
Head Office restock view for May — across all 8 accessible stores, the strongest May-to-summer replenishment candidates are driven by stable demand, recent momentum, and low stockout risk. Overall sales were still rising into 2026: May units reached 9,940 vs 8,887 in May 2025 (+11.8% YoY), while June/July store patterns show the biggest demand concentration in Seattle, Online, and Tacoma.

  • 1) Ratcheting Screwdriver (SKU: HTSD050001) — Feb-Jul units: 39, 24, 21, 44, 48, 38. It peaked in June at 48 units, then softened to 38 in July, but still sits +23.1% above February. Inventory coverage is healthy, yet this is the clearest broad-demand hand tool to keep topped up for May.
  • 2) Finishing Hammer 13oz (SKU: HTHM041300) — Feb-Jul units: 27, 36, 43, 37, 28, 39. Demand rebounded strongly in July to 39 units, which is +39.3% vs June and +44.4% vs February. This looks like a good May restock candidate ahead of summer projects.
  • 3) Level 24-inch (SKU: HTMT000015) — Feb-Jul units: 37, 39, 38, 37, 35, 38. This is the steadiest item in the set, staying in a tight 35–39 unit range with a mild recovery in July. It is a safe, predictable replenishment item rather than a spike-driven one.
  • 4) Locking Pliers 10-inch (SKU: HTPL000008) — Feb-Jul units: 42, 29, 20, 44, 40, 40. After dipping to 20 units in April, demand recovered to 44 in May and held at 40 in June/July. This suggests a rebound pattern worth restocking, but not as aggressively as the top 3.
  • 5) Metric Hex Key Set (SKU: HTAK000018) — Feb-Jul units: 27, 23, 39, 50, 40, 29. It peaked in May at 50 units, then fell to 29 by July. Because the trend is fading after a spring spike, this should be a lower-priority restock unless you want to protect against another short-term peak.

Inventory note: current stock is still substantial across the network, so this is a preventive May replenishment call rather than an urgent shortage response. The lowest observed stock among these items is still not critical (for example, Level 24-inch is 84 in Spokane and 90 in Kirkland), while Online and Seattle hold the largest positions.

Bottom line: prioritize Ratcheting Screwdriver and Finishing Hammer 13oz first, then maintain steady supply of Level 24-inch and Locking Pliers 10-inch; treat Metric Hex Key Set as a cautious, lower-priority restock due to post-peak decline.

title.text: Monthly Sales Performance for Top 5 Products Across All Stores (Feb-Jul)

components.content:
Methodology note: Sales trends were evaluated by aggregating retail.orders and retail.order_items by month, then comparing units sold and revenue across the available February–May history (and June–July where store detail was provided). Year-over-year seasonality was assessed by matching the same month across prior years. Restock priority was determined from current inventory on hand versus recent monthly demand, with higher priority assigned to items showing stronger recent sales momentum and lower stock coverage.

Head Office perspective: Across the chain, February–May sales have grown materially since 2020. For example, February units increased from 6,357 in 2020 to 10,008 in 2026, while February revenue rose from $476,692.13 to $763,329.92. The same pattern holds in March–May, indicating a broad upward trend rather than isolated store noise.

  • 2026 vs 2025: February units were up 13.3% (10,008 vs 8,834) and revenue up 18.5% ($763,329.92 vs $644,240.11).
  • Seasonality: March and April remain strong months, but revenue growth is not perfectly linear; e.g., 2026 revenue eased from $763,329.92 in February to $650,763.49 in March and $640,041.68 in April, suggesting mix/discount effects alongside volume growth.
  • Store mix: In 2024, the largest monthly contributors were Seattle and Online. February 2024 units were 2,415 in Seattle and 2,242 Online, versus 1,590 in Bellevue and 1,128 in Tacoma.

Restock methodology: Priority was based on recent demand trend and inventory coverage. For the top tracked items, current stock is still healthy across all 8 accessible stores, so the main signal is demand momentum rather than stockout risk. Example: Ratcheting Screwdriver sold 39, 24, 21, 44, 48, 38 units from Feb–Jul, with revenue peaking at $1,829.76 in June; despite softer July sales, it remains the highest restock priority because of broad demand and recent strength. By contrast, Metric Hex Key Set peaked in May at 50 units and then fell to 29 in July, so it is the lowest restock priority.

Inventory context: The sampled products are well covered: Level 24-inch has 224 units across 6 months of sales (~37.3/month), Locking Pliers 10-inch has 215 units (~35.8/month), and Ratcheting Screwdriver has 214 units (~35.7/month). Even the lowest observed store stock in the sample, 84 units for Level 24-inch in Spokane, is not an immediate stockout signal.
